messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: unusual auth traffic to auth-proxy observed from 52.12.34.0/24 starting ~12:34 UTC. 401 rate x20 baseline, top path /api/v1/sessions/validate. Pager routed to on-call marta. Sev: P2.

marta: I'm up. quick summary? scope + customer impact?

incident-bot: Summary: 12:34–12:40 spike in 401/403s. Affected: auth-proxy, tokenservice, sso-edge. Top client ASN: AS14618. Sample log lines (sanitized):
```
[12:35:11] auth-proxy INFO method=POST path=/api/v1/sessions/validate status=401 src=52.12.34.21 hdrs={"Authorization":"Bearer eyJhbGci...","User-Agent":"curl/7.68.0"}
[12:35:13] tokenservice WARN issuer=svc-auth-edge token_id=tok-9a2f used_by=52.12.34.21 status=403
```

rahul: I see repeated bearer tokens from that /24. They look like long-lived service tokens issued to svc-auth-edge. Pulling token usage and recent issues now.

carol: security oncall. If these are service tokens, treat as possible credential leak. Temporary network block for the /24, preserve logs, rotate affected service keys. I'll coordinate with legal if any PII appears.

marta: Applying temporary block to stop ongoing abuse. Executing cloud firewall block.

marta: ```bash
# gcloud example (replace with AWS equivalent if needed)
gcloud compute firewall-rules create block-suspicious-2487654321 \
  --direction=INGRESS --action=DENY \
  --source-ranges=52.12.34.0/24 \
  --target-tags=auth-proxy --description="temp block for incident 2487654321"
```

deployment-bot: Firewall rule block-suspicious-2487654321 created by marta at 12:46 UTC.

rahul: Confirmed: traffic from 52.12.34.0/24 dropped ~95%. Still seeing retries via proxied hosts in same ASN from different addresses. Dumping token activity for svc-auth-edge:
```
$ rbx auth tokens list --service svc-auth-edge --since 2h
TOK_ID    LAST_USED_BY    STATUS
tok-9a2f  52.12.34.21     active
tok-3f11  34.201.12.3      active
```

marta: If tok-9a2f is leaked we need immediate rotation + revoke. Carol, can sec do rotation now and coordinate deploy?

carol: On it. Plan:
- revoke tok-9a2f and any tokens with same issuer immediately
- create replacement token for svc-auth-edge with short TTL
- update deploy configs and roll to auth-proxy + tokenservice canaries
ETA ~15m

ben: any customer-facing impact yet? I see a small uptick in SSO failures on Kibana dashboards but no 5xx spike.

marta: No customer outage. Some customers may see auth failures (~3–7% in certain regions). Will open bridge if >10% sustained.

carol: Revoke command (internal tool):
```
$ rbx auth tokens revoke --token tok-9a2f --reason "suspected leakage 2487654321"
Revoke queued -> success
```

rahul: Snapshotting auth logs and pushing evidence to secure bucket.
```bash
# ES snapshot
curl -XPUT https://es.internal/_snapshot/inc-2487654321 -d '{"indices":"auth-logs-*","ignore_unavailable":true}'
aws s3 cp /tmp/es-snapshot-2487654321.tar.gz s3://redwood-incident-evidence/2487654321/ --acl=private
```

marta: Rotation completed, new token created and deployed to canary, auth-proxy canaries report normal auth behavior. Monitoring now.

rahul: Post-block metrics: 401s down to baseline within 7 minutes. Token usage for revoked tok-9a2f shows no new hits after revoke. Still flagging other tokens issued in same window for review.

carol: Legal/PR notified with initial incident brief. No confirmed data exfil. Preserve logs for 90 days.

marta: Next steps:
- full token sweep for svc-auth-* tomorrow morning
- incident review + root cause analysis (probable secret exfil from staging -> prod misconfig or third-party dev box)
- rotate any long-lived service tokens where feasible

dave: ack taking night-monitoring. I'll watch auth error rates and token audit.

incident-bot: STATUS UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. Follow-up: postmortem scheduled 2024-04-18 17:00 UTC. Tags: security, auth, rotation.

marta: Thanks team. Leaving follow-up items in #incidents-postmortem. Closing active pager. :white_check_mark:
